Permutation test for trait-specific module recurrence

Source: R/tag_permutation.R
tag_permutation.Rd

Tests whether HOGs recur in trait-specific modules across independent species pairs more than expected by chance. The null swaps the two trait labels within each pair, re-tags diverged modules – those whose topology is not preserved in the partner network – and counts HOG recurrence under the relabelled design.

tag_permutation(
  classification,
  modules,
  orthologs,
  pairs,
  group,
  target_group,
  n_perm = 1000L,
  min_recurrence = NULL,
  statistic = c("count", "excess"),
  universe = NULL,
  enum_max = 20L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

classification

Data frame from preservation_paired()$classification. Must contain columns pair_name, module, reference, test and classification. reference names the species whose modules the row describes and test the partner network they were tested in; classification is one of "conserved", "moderate", "diverged" or "untested", and only "diverged" rows contribute. Preservation only reports modules with at least min_module_size mapped genes, so the HOG pool is smaller than the retired gene-overlap engine's.

modules

Named list of detect_modules outputs. Names must include all species referenced by pairs.

orthologs

Data frame with columns Species1, Species2, hog.

pairs

Data frame with columns sp1, sp2, and pair_name, matching the contrasts in classification.

group

Named character vector mapping species identifiers to trait values (e.g., c(BDIS = "annual", BSYL = "perennial")). All species in pairs must have entries.

target_group

Character string: the trait value to test recurrence for (e.g., "annual").

n_perm

Number of labellings to draw when the null is too large to enumerate (default 1000). Only used when the label space exceeds 2^enum_max, which needs 21 independent contrast groups at the default — 42 species if they are disjoint — so in practice the null is always enumerated and this argument is ignored, with a message when it was supplied explicitly. Enumeration is decided on cost rather than on n_perm so that raising n_perm for precision cannot demote the null from exact to sampled. See enum_max to lower that ceiling.

min_recurrence

Minimum number of pairs in which a HOG must appear to be counted as recurring. NULL (default) uses half the contributing contrasts, at least 2 — which is 2 for a four-contrast design, so small designs behave as they did when the default was the constant 2. A constant does not describe a design of arbitrary size. Writing p for the chance that one HOG falls in a diverged module on one side of one pair, a HOG reaches at least 2 of k target sides by chance alone with probability 1 - (1 - p)^k - k p (1 - p)^(k - 1). At the p = 0.08 of the eight-species Pooideae set that is about 0.03 at k = 4 and 0.19 at k = 10: the statistic saturates on chance recurrence, and simulation shows power becoming non-monotone in k and collapsing by k = 10. Scaling it as max(2, round(k / 2)) restores monotone power, and is what NULL does. Exceeding the number of contributing pairs is an error: no HOG could recur in that many, so the statistic would be 0 under every labelling. At min_recurrence = 1 the statistic degenerates to the size of the union of the chosen sides, a pure set-size measure.

statistic

Either "count" (default) or "excess". Inference is exact under both — the permutation null is recomputed on whichever is chosen — so this is a power choice, not a validity one. observed is the recurrence count either way and statistic_observed is the value actually tested.

"count" is the raw number of recurring HOGs. It scales with how many HOGs the selected sides happen to hold, so a contrast whose two sides differ greatly in size dominates the null, which then ranks labellings largely by set size. Measured on the eight-species Pooideae set, 98\ the total size of the selected sides.

"excess" subtracts the count expected from independent sides of exactly those sizes, as a Poisson-binomial upper tail over universe. Whether this helps depends on the regime, and it can make matters worse. It works when the sides are small relative to the universe — on the Pooideae set it cuts the variance explained by set size from 0.98 to 0.33 and moves the observed labelling from 6th to 3rd of 16. It over-corrects when the sides between them account for most of the universe, because the independence model then predicts far more overlap than disjoint sides can produce: on a simulated design whose sides nearly partition the universe, the size dependence rises rather than falls (measured 0.97 to 0.999 as the sides were made more disjoint). Check $pair_sizes against universe before trusting it, and treat a large negative statistic_observed as a sign that the universe is too small.

universe

Reference universe for statistic = "excess": a count, or a vector of HOG identifiers whose distinct values are counted. Defaults to every HOG in orthologs. This is not identifiable from the data — it is the set of HOGs that could have appeared in a diverged module, which the data cannot report — and the correction is sensitive to it, so it is an argument rather than something inferred. A universe at or below the union of the selected sides forces the expectation above what disjoint sides can deliver and drives the statistic systematically negative. Ignored for statistic = "count".

enum_max

Enumerate while the label space holds at most 2^enum_max labellings (default 20). That is 2^enum_max serial evaluations of the statistic in the worst case — about a million at the default, which on Pooideae-sized HOG pools is tens of minutes — so lower it to fall back to n_perm sampled draws when that cost is not worth an exact p-value. Values above 30 are refused.

seed

Integer seed for the sampled branch, or NULL (default) to draw from the ambient RNG stream and leave it advanced. A seed draws from a private stream and restores the caller's on exit, the package-wide contract described under detect_modules. An enumerated null draws nothing, so a seed changes nothing there.

Value

A list with components:

observed

Integer: number of HOGs recurring in >= min_recurrence pairs for target_group.

null_distribution

Integer vector of recurrence counts under the null: all 2^k labellings when exact is TRUE, otherwise n_perm sampled ones.

p_value

One-sided p-value, comparing statistic_observed — not observed — against null_distribution, which is a double vector. When exact is TRUE this is mean(null >= statistic_observed) over the complete null, which already includes the observed labelling; when sampled it is (sum(null >= statistic_observed) + 1) / (n_perm + 1). The comparison carries a tolerance, since under statistic = "excess" mathematically tied labellings need not be bitwise equal.

p_min

Smallest p-value this design can produce (2^-k when enumerated, 1 / (n_perm + 1) when sampled). A p_value above alpha is uninformative when p_min is also above it.

p_attainable

The floor after ties: labellings sharing a statistic cannot be separated, so nothing scores below the tail of the maximum. Equals p_min when the maximum is unique, and whenever the null was sampled.

statistic

Echo of the input.

statistic_observed

The observed value of the chosen statistic — what null_distribution is compared against. Equals observed when statistic = "count".

n_labellings

Size of the admissible label space, the product over components, which is 2^k: a component with at least one contrast admits at most two labellings, since the seed species can only carry one of that contrast's two labels.

n_contributing

Number of pairs feeding the statistic — those with exactly one side in target_group. Exceeds n_swappable both when contrasts are coupled into one component and when a component's labellings all select the same HOG sets.

exact

Logical: was the null enumerated?

n_swappable

The k above: the number of components some relabelling moves, not a count of pairs. For a disjoint design the two coincide.

pair_sizes

Data frame with one row per contrast and columns pair_name, sp1, sp2, n_hogs_sp1, n_hogs_sp2, contributes, block, swappable, n_hogs_target and n_hogs_partner. The last two are NA on rows that do not contribute, since those have no target side. block gives the component each contrast belongs to and swappable is a property of that component, so it is TRUE for every contrast in a component some relabelling moves. The relabelling is exchangeable only if the target side is not systematically the larger one; if it is, the statistic reads set size rather than recurrence.

size_asymmetry_p

One-sided sign-test p-value for the target side being the larger one across the non-tied contrasts in components some relabelling moves. A warning is emitted when it is at or below 0.10 — an advisory threshold, since like p_min this cannot reach 0.05 below five pairs. NA when every swappable pair is tied. This is a diagnostic on the null's exchangeability assumption, not part of the test.

recurrence_table

Data frame with columns hog and n_pairs: observed per-HOG recurrence counts (only HOGs appearing in at least 1 pair).

target_group

Echo of the input.

min_recurrence

The threshold actually used — the resolved value, not an echo, when the input was NULL.

n_perm

Number of null values actually used.

Null model

The design is a randomised block: the pair is the block, the two species in it are the two levels of the trait, and the pairs are the unit of replication. The null hypothesis is that which member of a pair carries target_group is unrelated to which of its modules diverge. Under that hypothesis the trait label is exchangeable within a pair and not across pairs, so each draw independently either swaps a pair's two labels or leaves them alone. Module structure and gene content are held fixed.

A pair contributes HOGs for target_group only when exactly one of its two species carries that trait. Every swap preserves each pair's pair of labels, so a pair that contributes under the observed labelling contributes under every draw — the null stays inside the design that was actually run.

A component counts toward k only when relabelling it changes the statistic. A contrast whose two species share a label is pinned; with three or more trait values a contrast whose labels differ but where neither is the target contributes nothing under either orientation; and a component whose labellings all select the same HOG sets — most often one with no diverged module above min_module_size on either side — adds no resolution. Counting any of these would multiply the label space without separating anything, and p_min would then claim a floor the design cannot reach. The label space is enumerated exactly while it holds at most 2^enum_max labellings, and n_perm is then ignored; beyond that n_perm labellings are drawn, one admissible labelling per component. Either way the observed labelling is one of the points, so the smallest attainable p-value is p_min (2^-k when enumerated). A design with fewer than 5 independent contrast groups cannot reach p < 0.05 no matter how strong the signal, because 2^-4 = 0.0625. The function warns whenever max(p_min, p_attainable) exceeds 0.05, naming whichever of the two — too small a label space, or ties within it — actually binds.

Because a swap of every pair maps the statistic for one trait value onto the statistic for the other, running the test for two complementary trait values reads two entries of the same null distribution. Those are not independent tests and must not be corrected as if they were.

Contrasts sharing a species are coupled: relabelling one changes the other, so they cannot be swapped independently. The unit of independence is therefore the connected component of the graph whose nodes are species and whose edges are contrasts, and the null is the product over components of each component's admissible labellings. A component's labelling is fixed by the label given to any one of its species, since each contrast then forces its partner, so enumerating the alphabet for one species and propagating finds them all. A disjoint pairing gives one component per contrast with two labellings each, which is where 2^k comes from — the special case, not the assumption. The test generalises to any number of trait values with arbitrary frequencies, to unbalanced designs, and to species appearing in several contrasts.

An earlier version permuted trait labels across all species without conditioning on the pairing. That null mixed the observed design with designs having fewer contributing pairs (for four pairs, 77\ support), which inflated its variance and made it anti-conservative.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
mod_results <- preservation_paired(modules, networks, orthologs,
  pairs = data.frame(
    sp1 = c("BDIS", "HVUL"),
    sp2 = c("BSYL", "HJUB"),
    pair_name = c("Brachypodium", "Hordeum")
  ),
  group = c(
    BDIS = "annual", BSYL = "perennial",
    HVUL = "annual", HJUB = "perennial"
  )
)

result <- tag_permutation(
  mod_results$classification, modules, orthologs,
  pairs = data.frame(
    sp1 = c("BDIS", "HVUL"),
    sp2 = c("BSYL", "HJUB"),
    pair_name = c("Brachypodium", "Hordeum")
  ),
  group = c(
    BDIS = "annual", BSYL = "perennial",
    HVUL = "annual", HJUB = "perennial"
  ),
  target_group = "annual"
)
result$p_value
} # }
